name: Doxy.me
description: Doxy.me is a browser-based telehealth platform with provider waiting rooms, patient check-in, encrypted video visits, chat, invitations and clinic administration. Patients join through a provider's link without an account or download, while healthcare providers use registered free or paid accounts to host sessions.
agentUseSummary: Doxy.me cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because its public integration material describes support-enabled meeting-history, webhook, EHR and embedding features without publishing the complete stable authentication, endpoint, schema, signature and credential contract needed for a safe healthcare integration. Relay will not substitute provider login credentials, patient room links or browser automation for that contract.

blocked.label: Connect a Doxy.me provider account
blocked.description: Relay does not collect provider usernames, passwords, Google sign-in authority, SSO assertions, MFA codes, session cookies, clinic administrator access or patient room URLs.

blocked.label: Automate patient telehealth workflows
blocked.description: Relay does not create or alter invitations, append patient identifiers or names to room links, auto-check patients in, manage waiting rooms, start calls, send chat or files, capture photos, collect payments or automate the provider dashboard.

blocked.label: Use meeting history or session webhooks
blocked.description: Relay does not guess unpublished API endpoints or credentials, configure support-gated integrations, accept unsigned or unverified session events, or process meeting history until Doxy.me supplies a reviewed tenant-specific contract.

blocked.label: Embed telehealth sessions
blocked.description: Relay does not embed provider sign-in, patient rooms or custom Doxy.me URLs, provision clinical users, or present video-session hosting as a bounded agent action.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No action is exposed until Doxy.me provides an approved integration contract and the customer establishes the required healthcare plan, support enablement, BAA and least-privilege technical credentials.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay mounts no Doxy.me provider login, room link, patient identifier, meeting-history API, webhook, embedded session or health data in OpenClaw.
Relay mounts no Doxy.me provider login, room link, patient identifier, meeting-history API, webhook, embedded session or health data in Hermes.

providerSetup.blocker: Doxy.me's public help describes legacy Clinic integrations for patient identifiers, auto check-in, EHR launch, meeting history and session webhooks, but directs new Premium customers to authenticated support for current integration information. It does not publicly establish the complete production API base URL, credential issuance and revocation process, tenant binding, resource schemas, authorization model, webhook registration and signature verification, versioning, limits or support guarantees Relay needs. The embeddable SDK hosts Doxy.me pages inside another healthcare application rather than granting a bounded server-side management API. Doxy.me provider accounts use interactive login or configured SSO, patients join through provider room links without accounts, and those identities are not reusable Railway credentials. The workflows may contain patient identifiers, appointment and session metadata, protected health information and clinical communications, while Doxy.me's terms place patient consent, professional obligations and lawful care on the provider. Safe implementation therefore also requires an eligible clinic agreement, BAA, data-flow review and approved minimum-purpose action map.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request provider credentials, SSO assertions, patient names or identifiers, room links, cookies, webhook secrets, meeting-history tokens, clinic settings or health data; contact support as the user; enable integrations; sign a BAA; embed sessions; automate the dashboard; or show Connect. Reconsider when an authorized Doxy.me clinic supplies current official API and webhook documentation, plan entitlement, BAA and data-processing approval, tenant-scoped non-human credentials, exact endpoints and schemas, signed-event verification, revocation and rotation, test tenancy, rate limits, retention rules and explicit permission for Relay's bounded use.

evidence.supports: Doxy.me documents browser-based telehealth where providers sign in to registered accounts and patients join a provider's waiting-room link without an account or download.

Doxy.me describes legacy Clinic patient identifiers, auto check-in, EHR launch, meeting-history API and session webhooks, while directing current Premium integration questions to authenticated support.
Doxy.me lists EHR-adjacent integrations that its team can help implement, including patient identifiers, SSO, EHR launch and session webhooks.

Doxy.me presents its embeddable SDK as browser embedding for provider sign-in and patient rooms and says healthcare customers must validate room identifiers, authenticate access and handle compliance.
Doxy.me distinguishes provider and patient data, describes transient handling of files, photos and invitations, and documents healthcare-sensitive privacy and service-provider data flows.
Doxy.me requires providers to comply with healthcare laws and remain responsible for patient agreements, consent, professional services, billing and other patient interactions.
